newsitem.title: USA: Boston Co says Middlesex Cty, Mass defaulted.
newsitem.headline: Boston Co says Middlesex Cty, Mass defaulted.

text.p: Boston Co, part of Mellon Bank Corp, said on Friday that Middlesex County, Massachusetts, home of Harvard University, had defaulted on $3 million of notes that it owned and that were due on Friday.
"They were due today, so technically, that would be the case," said Vincent Loporchio, a company spokesman.
The spokesman added that the company was in close contact with county and state officials. "We're hopeful that the situation will be resolved soon."

Dreyfus, another Mellon unit, owns the notes in the Basic Massachusetts Money Market Fund and the Municipal Reserve Fund. The notes are a fairly small portion of the funds' holdings, and Mellon manages more than $200 billion.

Middlesex, the state's largest county, ran into trouble because it is selling a hospital, a deal expected to close five days after the notes were due, but the proceeds and remaining receivables will not be enough to meet all hospital-related liabilities.

A state emergency board early this afternoon refused to authorize the county's request to borrow about $6 million to repay the $4.5 million of notes and interest. The rest of the $4.5 million issue is owned by Fleet Financial Group, which said it expected to get notice of a default on Monday.
